title: HAVING AVG
flavorText: HAVING works with any aggregate — not just COUNT. HAVING AVG(price) > threshold filters groups by their mean.
narrative: Find categories where the average product price is above 50 credits — the premium segments.
schemaSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL, stock INTEGER NOT NULL);
seedSql: INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Datapad','Electronics',299.99,45),(2,'Power Cell','Electronics',19.99,200),(3,'Steel Cable','Hardware',8.50,500),(4,'Logic Board','Electronics',89.99,30),(5,'Ceramic Fuse','Hardware',2.25,1000),(6,'Optic Lens','Optics',149.99,15),(7,'Servo Motor','Robotics',55.00,80),(8,'Pressure Valve','Hardware',12.75,300);
task: Find categories where the average price exceeds 50. Show category and avg_price, ordered by avg_price descending.

hints.text: Use GROUP BY category HAVING AVG(price) > 50.
SELECT category, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING AVG(price) > 50 ORDER BY avg_price DESC;
SELECT category, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING AVG(price) > 50 ORDER BY avg_price DESC;
